notes: Both coders coded the same three university-layer documents (AI for Students page, DELTA course-guidelines article, Graduate Handbook AI policy) with the same stances (delegates, delegates, permit). Most disagreement was phase (boundaries between course-start, before-course, general and during-work for guidance statements; resolved by asking when in the work the advice applies and whether it communicates rules to students). Next came unit_stance on accountability and verification duties (set to neutral, because 'require' means AI use is required), and a few type choices (P31 vs UNCOVERED, P32 vs P12, P77 vs P45, P71 vs UNCOVERED, P36 vs P28/P62, P66 vs P09), resolved by re-reading the source: UNCOVERED kept where no type fits (calibrating on familiar subjects, group agreement), a type assigned where its definition covers the case (P71). Single-coder units were checked against the source: kept ones are real rules, caution or limitation statements, or enforcement of disclosure; dropped ones are a provenance sentence about how DELTA drafted its samples and an APA citation example, neither of which is a policy. Normalized policy text was kept only where the anchor alone does not state the rule.
